text.text: This page is where the practice keeps its calendar honest: clients and engagements, the monthly close for each, the filing deadlines coming up and the documents still owed. It tracks work only and gives no tax or financial advice. Start on the Dashboard, then work Overdue and Mine.
Clients
The businesses, nonprofits and households the firm serves.
Monthly closes
One close per client per month, from documents in to package delivered.
Filing deadlines
Tax and compliance dates the firm prepares and files for each client.
Document requests
Documents the firm has asked each client to send.

This workspace runs the client side of a bookkeeping and accounting firm: who each client is and what you do for them, every monthly close and where it stands, every filing deadline, and the documents you are waiting for. The books themselves stay in each client's accounting software; this is where the firm sees the whole workload.

No work without a signed engagement letter.
Every deadline is in the list the day the client signs, for the whole year ahead.
A close is delivered only after review by a second person.

text.text: Example

Alder & Vine's close is a day late with five questions for the owner and the bank still not reconciled. The preparer sends the questions in one email this morning and books a ten-minute call so the close can go out this week.
Busy season
From January to April, tax work takes over. Agree with bookkeeping clients in December which closes may run a few days later during those months, and say so in writing.

text.text: A monthly close turns a month of transactions into numbers an owner can trust. Doing it the same way every month, for every client, is what makes it fast and reliable.
The close checklist
Bank and credit card feeds complete for the month
Every bank and card account reconciled to the statement; tick
Statements reconciled
Uncategorized transactions cleared; the count goes in
Unreconciled items
Payroll entries match the payroll report
Payables and receivables aged and reviewed; tick
Payables and receivables reviewed
Loan balances agree with lender statements
Sales tax collected agrees with the sales tax return
Fixed asset purchases and depreciation recorded
Questions for the client listed in one place; the count in
Questions for the client
The stages
Review

The reviewer looks at the balance sheet first: cash matches the bank, no odd balances, no negative payables. Then the profit and loss against the last three months: anything that jumped or vanished gets a question.
Delivering the close
Send the profit and loss, balance sheet and a short note: three things the owner should know this month.
Send all open questions in that same email.
Set
Delivered
with the date.
When numbers look wrong
If a balance cannot be explained, do not force it. Park the difference in a clearly named suspense account, list it as a question for the client, and clear it next month. Hidden differences grow.
Due dates
Most firms promise closes by the 15th.
Documents due
is usually the 5th; if documents are late, the close date moves the same number of days, and the client is told.
Example
Cedar Hollow's close is still waiting on bank statements that were due a day ago. The bookkeeper sends one reminder through the portal and moves on to Brightwater Dental, which is ready for review.
A missed filing means penalties, interest and an unhappy client, and often the firm pays. The deadline list is the firm's most important list, and it is complete for the year ahead.
Setting up each client
When a client signs, add every deadline for the next twelve months:

An extension gives more time to file, not to pay. Estimate what is owed and tell the client to pay by the original date. Tick

Example
Pinecone Playschool's state registration renewal is three days overdue. The preparer files it today, notes the late fee for the client, and adds next year's renewal to the list straight away.
Busy season planning
In December, list every return due between January and April with its preparer. If one person has too many, move work early rather than in March.
When the client must act
Many deadlines need the client to sign or pay. Send the request at least a week ahead with the amount and the exact steps, and call if it is not done two days before.
The first month with a client sets up every month after. A clean start means accurate opening balances, a complete deadline list and a client who knows what to send and when.

Loan agreements, leases and fixed asset records
Add each as a document request with a due date.

Fiscal year ends
Review the books: bank balances, uncategorized items, payables and receivables. Note what needs cleaning up.
Agree opening balances with the prior accountant's numbers.
Add every deadline for the year ahead.
Add the first monthly close with a documents due date.
The kickoff call
Walk through the monthly rhythm: what they send by the 5th, what they get by the 15th.
Show them the portal and how to answer questions.
Agree one contact person on their side.
The first month
Expect the first close to take twice as long as later ones. Note what slowed it down, and fix those things before the second month.
Clean-up work
If the books need months of catch-up, quote it separately from the monthly fee. Catch-up work underpriced as part of the monthly fee is the most common money loser for bookkeeping firms.
Example

Pinecone Playschool is onboarding without a signed engagement letter, and its prior year return is still not in after three reminders. The owner of the firm calls the director to get both done before any bookkeeping starts.
Most late closes and late returns are waiting on the client. A polite, consistent chasing routine gets documents in without damaging the relationship.
Asking well
Ask for everything in one list, not one item at a time.
Say exactly what you need: "Statements for every bank account, all pages, for last month."
Give a due date and how to send it:
Send it by
portal, email or paper drop-off.
Explain why it matters: "We need this to finish your close by the 15th."
The reminder rhythm

cells.text: Second reminder, with what is delayed
Phone call from the client manager
Note to the partner; agree new dates in writing

text.text: Count each reminder in
Reminders sent
and set the status to
Reminded
When it arrives
Check it is complete: every account, every page, the right dates.
Set
Received
with the date.
Thank the client; short and warm.
Make it easy
Bank feeds and automatic statement downloads remove most monthly requests.
A standing monthly list (statements, receipts over an agreed amount, payroll report) means clients know what to send without being asked.
Paper drop-off is fine for clients who prefer it; scan it the same day.
When a client is always late
Talk about it at renewal. Offer a later close date, a higher fee for the extra chasing, or a simpler service. Record what you agreed on the client.
Example
Cedar Hollow's bank statements are two days past due after two reminders. The client manager calls the treasurer, who forgot the portal login, and the statements arrive within the hour.
Year-end lists
In November, send every client the list of year-end documents: tax forms, donation receipts, asset purchases and loan statements. Early lists mean fewer late returns.
Privacy
Never ask for documents or passwords by plain email for sensitive data. Use the portal, and never store client passwords in notes.
